answer_text:
Let \(A,B,C\) be the angles of the triangle, so

\[
A+B+C=180^\circ,\qquad A,B,C>0.
\]

Let

\[
s=\sin(kC).
\]

Since \(s\le 1\) and \(\sin A,\sin B>0\), we have

\[
\cos A\cos B+\sin A\sin B\,s
\le \cos A\cos B+\sin A\sin B.
\]

Using the cosine difference identity,

\[
\cos A\cos B+\sin A\sin B=\cos(A-B).
\]

Thus

\[
1=\cos A\cos B+\sin A\sin B\,s
\le \cos(A-B)\le 1.
\]

Therefore equality must hold throughout. Hence

\[
\cos(A-B)=1
\]

and the inequality involving \(s\) must also be equality, which requires

\[
s=\sin(kC)=1.
\]

Since \(A,B\in(0,180^\circ)\), we have \(|A-B|<180^\circ\), so

\[
\cos(A-B)=1 \implies A-B=0 \implies A=B.
\]

Thus the triangle must be isosceles with

\[
2A+C=180^\circ.
\]

So \(C\) must be even, because \(A=(180-C)/2\) is an integer.

Also,

\[
\sin(kC)=1.
\]

Since \(k\) is a positive integer and \(kC\le 360^\circ\), the only possibility is

\[
kC=90^\circ.
\]

Therefore \(C\) must be a positive integer divisor of \(90\), and \(C\) must be even.

The even divisors of \(90\) are

\[
2,6,10,18,30,90.
\]

For each such \(C\), we get a valid integer angle

\[
A=B=\frac{180-C}{2}.
\]

These give the similarity classes

\[
(89^\circ,89^\circ,2^\circ),
\]
\[
(87^\circ,87^\circ,6^\circ),
\]
\[
(85^\circ,85^\circ,10^\circ),
\]
\[
(81^\circ,81^\circ,18^\circ),
\]
\[
(75^\circ,75^\circ,30^\circ),
\]
\[
(45^\circ,45^\circ,90^\circ).
\]

Thus the number of distinct triangles up to similarity is

\[
\boxed{6}.
\]
